description: Four-panel composite figure of line plots that all share the same categorical x-axis labelled "Alloy (wt.%) Fe–30Mn–1.2C–" with ticks at 0Al, 2Al, 4Al, 6Al and 8Al. Each panel plots one mechanical property against Al content, with one coloured curve per aging condition: 550 °C, 24h (green); 600 °C, 1h (olive); 600 °C, 24h (dark red); 550 °C, 1h (yellow); 500 °C, 1h (red); 450 °C, 1h (blue); as-homogenised (black). (a) YS / MPa (gridlines 300–900 in 100 MPa steps): YS stays between roughly the 350 and 450 MPa lines from 0Al to 4Al, then climbs steeply to the 900 MPa gridline at 8Al for 550 °C, 24h; the blue 450 °C, 1h curve dips to its minimum at 6Al (annotated "450 °C, 1h") while as-homogenised rises to about the 500 MPa line at 8Al. (b) UTS / MPa (500–1000): the highest UTS is at 0Al (as-homogenised, above 800 MPa), falls to a minimum near 2Al (green, annotated "550 °C, 24h"), plateaus over 4–6Al and reaches about 1000 MPa at 8Al for 550 °C, 24h. (c) TE / % (10–80): the highest elongation, ~80%, is the as-homogenised condition at 0Al; TE drops to a minimum at 2Al and to near 10% at 8Al for 500 °C, 24h and 600 °C, 24h. (d) Hardness / HBW (150–400): flat ~200 HBW over 0–6Al, then a steep rise to about 375 HBW at 8Al. The four panels together show that strength and hardness increase while elongation decreases with rising Al content, with aging condition modulating the level.

subfigures.description: Line plot of YS / MPa versus Al content (0Al-8Al); values rise only slightly up to 4Al and then steeply, with the green 550 °C, 24h curve reaching the 900 MPa gridline at 8Al. A blue 450 °C, 1h curve shows a dip at 6Al, annotated '450 °C, 1h', and the black as-homogenised point at 6Al is annotated 'as-homogenised'.

Line plot of UTS / MPa versus Al content; the as-homogenised condition is highest at 0Al (above 800 MPa), all curves pass through a minimum near 2Al (the lowest green point annotated '550 °C, 24h'), plateau between 4Al and 6Al, and the 550 °C, 24h curve rises to ~1000 MPa at 8Al.

Line plot of TE / % versus Al content; elongation is highest at 0Al (~80% for as-homogenised), collapses at 2Al for the 550 °C, 24h condition (annotated), partly recovers at 4-6Al, and falls to ~10% at 8Al for 500 °C, 24h and 600 °C, 24h (both annotated).

Line plot of Hardness / HBW versus Al content; hardness is nearly flat around 200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al and then rises steeply towards the 375 HBW level at 8Al, the highest curve being 550 °C, 24h; the as-homogenised condition is annotated at 6Al.

observations.observation: The group consists of four line-plot panels labelled (a), (b), (c) and (d), all sharing the categorical x-axis 'Alloy (wt.%) Fe-30Mn-1.2C-' with ticks 0Al, 2Al, 4Al, 6Al, 8Al.
Panel (a) is plotted as YS / MPa with gridlines at 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800 and 900 MPa; panel (d) is plotted as Hardness / HBW with gridlines at 150, 200, 250, 300, 350 and 400 HBW.
Seven conditions are colour-coded in each panel legend: 550 °C, 24h; 600 °C, 1h; 600 °C, 24h; 550 °C, 1h; 500 °C, 1h; 450 °C, 1h; as-homogenised.
In (a), YS remains between roughly the 350 and 450 MPa gridlines from 0Al to 4Al and then rises steeply, the green 550 °C, 24h curve reaching the 900 MPa gridline at 8Al, the highest YS shown.

In (a) the blue 450 °C, 1h curve drops to a minimum at 6Al below the 400 MPa gridline, annotated '450 °C, 1h'; the black as-homogenised curve rises from about 400 MPa at 6Al to about the 500 MPa line at 8Al (annotated 'as-homogenised' near 6Al).

In (b) the highest UTS occurs at 0Al for the as-homogenised condition (above the 800 MPa gridline), and all curves pass through a low point near 2Al, the lowest being the green curve annotated '550 °C, 24h'.
In (b) the curves plateau between 4Al and 6Al and the green 550 °C, 24h curve reaches the 1000 MPa gridline at 8Al.

In (c) total elongation is highest for the as-homogenised condition at 0Al, near the 80% gridline, and falls to about the 10% gridline at 8Al for the 500 °C, 24h and 600 °C, 24h conditions (both annotated at 8Al).
In (c) the green 550 °C, 24h curve shows a pronounced minimum at 2Al, annotated '550 °C, 24h', while elongation recovers towards the 55-65% lines at 4-6Al for most conditions.
In (d) hardness stays around the 200 HBW gridline from 0Al to 6Al for all conditions and then increases steeply between 6Al and 8Al, the 550 °C, 24h curve reaching about the 375 HBW level.

A common pattern across the group is that the strength minimum in (a)/(b) at 2Al coincides with the elongation minimum in (c), and that the strength/hardness increase from 6Al to 8Al coincides with the elongation loss at 8Al.
No numeric data labels are printed on any curve; only axis tick values, condition labels and annotations such as '550 °C, 24h', '450 °C, 1h' and 'as-homogenised' are given.

The caption states that the panels show mechanical properties from RAP (Rapid Alloy Prototyping) experiments as a function of alloy composition and applied aging treatment: (a) yield stress (YS), (b) ultimate tensile stress (UTS), (c) total elongation (TE), (d) hardness.
The caption states that the data and figure are reproduced from an earlier publication (ref. 49).

The citing text states that Figure 3 shows the mechanical properties of 45 different material conditions for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C base composition, in total 135 tensile tests and hardness measurements, plotted according to systematically varied Al content with colour-coding reflecting the aging conditions.

unreadable_items: Colour-to-condition mapping is only partly resolvable: several curves use similar reds and greens, so individual points of e.g. 500 °C, 1h versus 550 °C, 1h (and 550 °C, 24h versus 600 °C, 1h) at intermediate Al levels cannot be unambiguously separated.
No numeric values are printed at the data points, so absolute property values can only be referenced to the printed axis gridlines.
